def:joint-packet.title: Finite source-complete joint packet
def:joint-packet.note: Encoded. RepresentedJointPacket (Lambda, V, M, E) bundles the represented data (J1)-(J5) in the coordinates of the central type decomposition: the common carrier is Carrier = Sigma lambda, (Fin 4 x V lambda) x M lambda (the paper's H_X up to the unitary decomposition of (J3), which the structure fixes as coordinates); (J1) the external Clifford factor M_4(C) acts as extAction a = blockDiagonal' (a (x) I (x) I), a unital *-representation (extAction_mul/one/conjTranspose) faithful when some sector is nonempty (extAction_injective); (J2)/(J3) A_int = ⊕ I_4 (x) B(V_lambda) (x) I_M is intAlgebra = range intAction (mem_intAlgebra_iff), commuting with A_ext (extAction_commute_intAction); (J4) the directed incidence graph is (src, tgt : E -> Lambda) with represented histories Y e : C^4 (x) V_{s e} (x) M_{s e} -> C^4 (x) V_{t e} (x) M_{t e}, placed on the (t e, s e) corner of the carrier by incidenceOp (blockEmbed); (J5) the mixed words are the elements of actionAlgebra = jointActionAlgebra A_ext A_int Y (def:action-algebra), star-closed; multiplicityAlgebra = its commutant. The earlier duality-facing SourceCompleteJointDualityPacket remains the packet used by thm:SMST-main-duality; linking the two (proving the commutant identities for a RepresentedJointPacket) is thm:main-duality, not this definition.

def:action-algebra.title: Joint typed action algebra
def:action-algebra.note: jointActionAlgebra Aext Aint Y : Subalgebra C (Matrix n n C) is C*(A_ext, A_int, Y_e, Y_e^* : e in E) on a common finite carrier, defined as starAdjoin (the unital *-subalgebra generated, i.e. the finite-dimensional C*-algebra generated) of A_ext ∪ A_int ∪ range Y with Y_e represented as matrices on the common carrier (extended by zero off the source/target blocks). Proved: A_ext, A_int, every Y_e and every Y_e^* lie in it, it is star-closed (so it fills the action_starClosed field of SourceCompleteJointDualityPacket), and it is the least star-closed unital subalgebra containing these generators (jointActionAlgebra_le), which characterises it as the C*-algebra of eq:joint-action-algebra. The typed packet data (J1)-(J5) are not re-encoded: Aext, Aint are taken as arbitrary sets of matrices.

thm:record-nonidentifiability.title: Classical record data do not determine the system algebra
thm:record-nonidentifiability.note: Proved (record_nonidentifiability). Statement: on any 20-dimensional carrier m (Fintype.card m = 20), for any record factor with Hermitian orthogonal projectors Q_a summing to I and any 0 <= theta <= 1, there exist two six-edge families K^c, K^q (the completions I/sqrt18 + (i/3) H of the commuting family H^c on the twenty three-subsets and of the Clifford family H^q = sqrt(6/5) sum_mu O_{e mu} Gamma_mu (x) I_5 on C^4 (x) C^5, both reindexed to m) such that: both satisfy eq:six-edge-normalization (sum K^*K = I, sum K = sqrt2 I, linear independence); both resolved instruments L_0 = sqrt(1-theta) I, L_{e,a} = sqrt(theta) K_e (x) Q_a (kraus) are normalized; they have the same one-step effects, the same effect L_w^* L_w for every classical word w (the same resolved record channel at every word length; the explicit eq:record-word-effect formula (1-theta)^{n_0}(theta/6)^m I (x) Q_a / zero for disagreeing types is record_word_effect), the same one-letter Hilbert-Schmidt Gram Tr K_e^* K_f, and Choi matrices with the same characteristic polynomial (choiMat_charpoly_eq_of_hsGram_eq via Matrix.charpoly_mul_comm': the Choi matrix is B B^* for the matrix B of Choi vectors, so its spectrum with multiplicities is a function of the Gram B^*B = Tr L_j^* L_k, which the two instruments share); yet the unital algebras generated by the K_e are not isomorphic (not Nonempty of an AlgEquiv) and neither are their commutants (Subalgebra.centralizer). New concrete inputs: a Helmert frame (helmert, integer Helmert vectors over sqrt(k(k+1))) and a Clifford family on C^4 (gamma 0..3 and the chirality). Renderings disclosed: C*(K_e) is taken as Algebra.adjoin of the K_e (the generators are I/sqrt18 + (i/3)H_e with H_e Hermitian, so the *-algebra equals the algebra; finite dimension); nonisomorphism is proved by the commutative/noncommutative contrast (adjoin K^c = diagonal algebra C^20 from the previous file; adjoin K^q contains Gamma_0 (x) I_5 and Gamma_1 (x) I_5; commutant of K^c = diagonal matrices, commutant of K^q contains I (x) M_5(C)); the exact identification C*(K^q) = M_4(C) (x) I_5 of eq:inequivalent-system-algebras and the explicit eigenvalue list eq:matching-Choi-spectrum are not computed (not needed for the countertheorem: 'same nonzero Choi spectrum' is covered by equality of the characteristic polynomials). The record factor is an arbitrary finite type with orthogonal projectors (the paper's four rank-one projectors are a special case); theta is allowed in the closed interval [0,1].

thm:pullback-reconstruction.title: Identity-pivot reconstruction of the system action
thm:pullback-reconstruction.note: Proved in full generality on a finite carrier Matrix n n C with a finite environment basis nu. coeffField C z = sum_nu conj(z_nu) C_nu is C(z) = (I ⊗ <z|)V; pullbackSet = {C(z)^* C(w)} are the pullbacks P^*(|z><w|) (eq:complementary-pullback is taken as the definition of the pullback, the isometry V and the complementary channel are left implicit); pullbackImage = their span = P^*(B(E)); pullbackAlgebra = C^*(P^*(B(E))). Hypotheses: Asys = starAdjoin (range C) = starAdjoin (range A) (i.e. A_sys = C*(C_nu) = C*(A_1..A_s)), C(z_0) = alpha • 1, C(z_j) = beta_j • A_j, alpha ≠ 0, beta_j ≠ 0. Conclusion: pullbackAlgebra C = Asys and matCommutant (pullbackAlgebra C) = matCommutant Asys, both clauses of eq:pullback-reconstruction. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

thm:word-module-recognition.title: Word-module recognition of historical internal actions
thm:word-module-recognition.note: Proved, and more generally than stated: for any unital C-algebra A (no finite-dimensionality, C*-structure or Wedderburn form needed; the statement is purely algebraic) and any family of algebra automorphisms alpha : G → (A ≃ₐ[C] A) (no group structure or finiteness of G needed), on the regular word carrier W = A with L_a = LinearMap.mulLeft, R_b = LinearMap.mulRight, U_g = (alpha g).toLinearMap: word_module_recognition states R(A)' ∩ U(G)' = L(A^G) as an equality of subsets of Module.End C A (commutants are Set.centralizer, A^G = invariantElements alpha = {a | ∀ g, alpha g a = a}, which is the fixed-point form of A ∩ {u_g}' for alpha_g = Ad(u_g)); word_module_recognition_iff is the 'equivalently' clause (T commutes with every R_b and every U_g iff T is left multiplication by a unique invariant element) and word_module_recognition_coefficient gives the coefficient T 1. The Hilbert-space structure of L^2(A, tau_reg) plays no role in the theorem and is not encoded (the carrier is the underlying vector space).

prop:word-module-defect.title: Exact module and symmetry defects
prop:word-module-defect.note: Proved. Setting: A a nontrivial finite-dimensional normed star ring over C with an inner product satisfying IsRegularTraceInner (<x,y> = tau_reg(x^* y) with tau_reg(z) = D^{-1} Tr_A(L_z), the intrinsic normalized regular trace formula of normalizedRegularTrace, equal to D^{-1} sum n_beta Tr(z_beta) in Wedderburn form); symmetries U_g = alpha_g given by a group hom alpha : G ->* (A ≃ₗᵢ[C] A) with alpha_g(1) = 1 (the paper's Ad(u_g) by unitaries is a special case, since tau_reg is tracial: regularTraceForm_mul_comm). hsNorm is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (l^2 norm of (S e_nu) over the standard orthonormal basis), proved basis-independent via LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner (hsNorm_sq_eq_sum). word_module_defect: ||T - L_{T1}||_HS = delta_R(T) (eq:word-module-defect, also squared form); groupAverage_identity: |G|^{-1} sum_g ||alpha_g a - a||^2 = 2||a - E_G a||^2; hsNorm_mulLeft_sq: ||L_b||_HS^2 = D||b||^2; word_module_invariant_defect: ||T - L_{E_G(T1)}||_HS <= delta_R(T) + sqrt(D/2) delta_G(T) (eq:word-module-invariant-defect); defects_vanish_iff: both defects vanish iff T = L_a with a G-invariant (the 'Thus' clause). Scoped hypotheses disclosed: Nontrivial A (D != 0), Nonempty G in the vanishing clause, alpha_g isometric and unital rather than inner.

cor:word-multiplicity-firewall.title: Word-space multiplicity firewall
cor:word-multiplicity-firewall.note: Proved in the scoped form recommended by the assessor: the corollary's mathematical content is witnessed on the paper's own twelve-root benchmark (Appendix prop:word-space-inflation: E = directed edges of K_4, S_4 relabeling matrices Pm, A = M_12). word_space_multiplicity_firewall: (i) the fixed points of the conjugation representation conjRep sigma X = P X P^{-1} on the word space L^2(M_12) are exactly the invariant algebra A^{S_4} = commutantSubmodule, so the trivial-representation multiplicity on the word space is finrank = 7 (commutant_finrank_eq_seven); (ii) the trivial multiplicity on the exposed physical carrier C^E is 1 (fixed vectors = constants, via S_4-transitivity on directed edges proved by decide); hence 'multiplicity on L^2(A) need not equal multiplicity on the physical carrier'; (iii) the word-space commutant contains an M_7(C) block: m7Block is an injective multiplicative linear embedding of Matrix (Fin 7) (Fin 7) C into End(L^2(M_12)) commuting with every conjRep sigma (built from the group average E_G and End(A^{S_4}) ≅ M_7); (iv) the physical invariant algebra A^{S_4} admits no injective linear image of M_3(C) (no_M3_embedding). Not formalised: the full multiplicity vectors (1,0,2,1,1) vs (7,5,19,17,12) for the non-trivial irreducibles (that is prop:word-space-inflation, a separate record) and the corollary's normative clauses ('must also pass thm:word-module-recognition', 'multiplicity-birth analysis refers to the physical carrier'), which are interpretive.

def:word-native-shadow.title: Word-native linear shadow
def:word-native-shadow.note: WordNativeShadow A records the declared data (m, c_alpha, A_alpha, B_alpha) and toLinearMap is the map X ↦ sum_alpha c_alpha A_alpha X B_alpha (toLinearMap_apply is eq:word-native-shadow pointwise); IsWordNative T := ∃ L, T = L.toLinearMap, with isWordNative_iff the explicit existential form. thm:external-shadow-no-go.title: Word moments cannot manufacture an external shadow
thm:external-shadow-no-go.note: Proved as a countermodel for an arbitrary finite old letter process K (h x Fin 2 resolved carrier, spectator two-level system, h nonempty). external_shadow_no_go packages: (i) both the even (clockZ) and odd (clockX) extensions recover every old word after normalized grading discard (conservative); (ii) the historical word algebras coincide literally (every extended old word is the same matrix), hence identical multiplication tables; (iii) the complete word-Gram hierarchies Tr(w1^H w2) coincide and equal twice the old Gram (trace_kronecker); (iv) all resolved entries of every historical word coincide (resolved cylinder data); (v) the proposed left-to-right grading cross block is 0 in the even extension and nonzero in the odd one; (vi)/(vii) no function of the historical word data, and no function of the word-Gram hierarchy, returns the cross block of both extensions. Scope: the grading-changing variant of the cross block is the instance exhibited (the theorem is existential, so one instance suffices); the typed-incidence variant is not separately modelled.

thm:factor-obstruction.title: Factor-commutant obstruction
thm:factor-obstruction.note: Every unital algebra map M_n(C) -> M_N(C) is conjugate (by an invertible unit, unitary equivalence left implicit) to a |-> a (x) I_k with N = n k, the commutant of M_I (x) 1 is exactly 1 (x) M_J, that commutant is a factor, and any set containing a non-scalar central element differs from it (nontrivial-centre obstruction). def:typed-multiplicity.title: Typed multiplicity algebra

Scope: undirected graph with orientation-pointwise edge data, as in the existing assembly file.

lem:multiplicity-factorization.title: Multiplicity-one incidence factorization
lem:multiplicity-factorization.note: Under the multiplicity-one hypothesis (every carrier intertwiner is uniquely a scalar multiple of D) an operator Y equivariant under L_q (x) 1 and R_q (x) 1 factorizes uniquely as Y = D (x) F. Matches the lemma with the typed symmetry given as an indexed family of matrix pairs.

thm:edge-commutant.title: Exact edge-commutant reconstruction
thm:edge-commutant.note: For a block family R (the form supplied by the trinity theorem) and nonzero typed carriers D_e, commuting with every loaded edge D_e (x) F_e and its adjoint is equivalent to the typed multiplicity equations on every edge of the graph, hence A_act' = M_type. def:support-polar.title: Support-polar action algebra
def:support-polar.note: Fresh definition on graph-indexed edge data (no copy of the excluded private file). Total carrier = Sigma v, M v over a finite vertex type; vertexProjection v = Z_v (orthogonal projections summing to 1, proved); blockEmbed places a rectangular block F_e : M_u -> M_v on the (v,u) corner; supportMetric = F_e^H F_e on the carrier; polarIsometry F is the canonical polar partial isometry U with F = U P, P psd, P^2 = F^H F, U U^H U = U and U^H U = supp P (existence transported from exists_singular_polar_data to arbitrary finite column types via Fintype.equivFin, then chosen); polarOp = U_e on the carrier; supportPolarAlgebra = StarAlgebra.adjoin of {Z_lambda, F_e^H F_e, U_e, U_e^H}. In finite dimension the algebraic star hull is the C*-hull, so this is O_F^sup. Scoped: SimpleGraph with orientation-pointwise edge data, as in GraphLoadedEdgeCommutantAssembly.

thm:support-polar.title: Exact support-polar duality
thm:support-polar.note: Proved on the general finite multi-vertex incidence graph (SimpleGraph G on a finite vertex type, oriented edge data F h : Matrix (M v) (M u) C arbitrary: rectangular, singular, rank-deficient or zero), on the total multiplicity carrier TotalCarrier M = Sigma v, M v of SupportPolarActionAlgebra.lean with the official supportPolarAlgebra (def:support-polar). M_type is represented as the block-diagonal matrices blockDiagonal' R with R in typedMultiplicityAlgebra (multiplicityCarrierAlgebra). exact_support_polar_duality = (M_type = (O^sup)') ∧ (O^sup = M_type') ∧ (C*(Z_lambda, F_e, F_e^*) = O^sup) i.e. eq:support-polar-duality and eq:incidence-support-polar-equality. Proof as in the paper: commuting with the Z_lambda forces block-diagonal form; per edge, commutation with F^*F, U, U^* on the (t,s) corner is polar_edge_singular (lem:polar-edge), whose support hypothesis is derived from the six polar identities (support_commute_of_polar_data, a range argument using commute_of_commute_sq); the reverse identity is double_commutant. The incidence/support-polar equality is obtained from the bicommutant theorem (both are star-closed unital algebras with commutant M_type) instead of the polynomial interpolation g(t)=t^{-1/2} of the paper's proof. The 'M_type' here is the multiplicity algebra on the multiplicity carrier only (the external/internal tensor factors of the full carrier are not part of thm:support-polar).

def:multiplicity-quiver.title: Multiplicity quiver

thm:quiver.title: Noncommuting-support quiver theorem
thm:quiver.note: Commutation of the central family (+) I_{V_a} (x) X_a with every assembled arrow T_j is proved equivalent to the blockwise quiver intertwining relations, giving the commutant/End Q equivalence, the Hilbert-Schmidt expansion of the commutator form into sum ||B X_a - X_b B||^2, and kernel = End Q. thm:polar-holonomy.note: With invertible edges F_e = U_e P_e (U_e unitary, P_e positive definite) and unitary root transports Q, the transported family R_lambda = Q_lambda R Q_lambda^* satisfies all typed edge equations iff R commutes with every K_e = Q^* P_e^2 Q and W_e = Q_t^* U_e Q_s; root transports exist along walks on a connected graph; the reverse identity O_F = (M^(o))' is finite bicommutant closure for star subalgebras.

thm:reciprocal-return.title: Finite reciprocal-return criterion
thm:reciprocal-return.note: Proved (reciprocal_return_criterion) at the paper's horizon n = dim N, for a finite group G with a unitary representation v (v(gg') = v g v g', v 1 = 1, v_g^* v_g = 1) whose commutant is scalar (Schur form of irreducibility), h self-adjoint, all index types finite, V nonempty. thm:central-separation.title: Central separation of the landed internal blocks
thm:central-separation.note: Proved on the concrete carrier C^7 = C^3+C^2+C+C where M_3+M_2+C+C is InternalAssemblyExact.blockAlgebra. central_separation: for a unital star-subalgebra B of M_7(C) contained in the block algebra whose colour corner (submatrix on {0,1,2}) is onto M_3(C) and whose weak corner (on {3,4}) is onto M_2(C) (surjectivity onto the two scalar factors is automatic from unitality), exactly one of B = blockAlgebra (finrank 15) or B = lockedAlgebra = {X block-diagonal, X_55 = X_66} (finrank 14) holds (Xor'). central_separation_criterion: for a bank b_j of block-diagonal generators with B = StarAlgebra.adjoin C (range b) satisfying the two corner surjectivities, B = blockAlgebra iff eta_cen = sum_j normSq(b_j 5 5 - b_j 6 6) > 0 (chi_1 = entry (5,5), chi_2 = entry (6,6)); etaCen_pos_of_central_projector: a represented scalar projector E_55 or E_66 in the bank forces eta_cen > 0. prop:main-det-incidence.title: Canonical determinant incidence

definition:determinant-seed.title: Determinant seed

thm:gauge-group.title: Gauge-group reconstruction
thm:gauge-group.note: SMGaugeGroup := ker(det A det B) inside U(3) x U(2) (= S(U(3) x U(2)), the seed stabilizer since (A,B) preserves tau iff det A det B = 1); the phase-weighted map Phi(g3,g2,z) = (z^-2 g3, z^3 g2) from SU(3) x SU(2) x U(1) is a surjective homomorphism with kernel exactly {(z^2 I_3, z^-3 I_2, z) : z^6 = 1} = Z_6, and the first isomorphism theorem gives the quotient isomorphism.

prop:operational-determinant-source.title: Positive operational source criterion for the determinant group
prop:operational-determinant-source.note: Proved. The marked positive subpacket is MarkedSectorPacket (two diagonal Choi blocks J00, J11 and the Choi cross block J01 : Matrix p q C); the hypothesis 'the group acts on the two sectors by the characters 1 and chi^{-1}' is encoded as the action packetAction (diagonal blocks invariant, cross block J01 |-> chi(g)^{-1} J01), and h_det := ||J01||_HS^2 (hDet). For a general group G and unitary character chi: h_det > 0 => stabilizer of the packet = ker chi; h_det = 0 => stabilizer = whole group. operational_determinant_source instantiates G = U(3) x U(2), chi = determinantProductHom: h_det > 0 => stabilizer = SMGaugeGroup = S(U(3) x U(2)); h_det = 0 => stabilizer = top and top != SMGaugeGroup (witness (-I_3, I_2), SMGaugeGroup_ne_top), i.e. the diagonal masses alone do not imply the determinant subgroup. Disclosed modelling choice: the character transformation law of the cross block is the definition of the action rather than derived from a Choi-matrix construction.

prop:faithful-SM-quotient.title: Faithful matter realization of the determinant quotient
prop:faithful-SM-quotient.note: Proved. The seven multiplets Q:(3,2)_1, u^c:(3bar,1)_-4, d^c:(3bar,1)_2, L:(1,2)_-3, e^c:(1,1)_6, H:(1,2)_3, nu^c:(1,1)_0 are realized as monoid homomorphisms from SMGaugeCover = (SU(3) x SU(2)) x Circle into matrix monoids (Kronecker product for Q, entrywise conjugation for 3bar, z^y phase with y = 6Y). commonKernel (intersection of the seven kernels) = smGaugeHom.ker = Subgroup.zpowers z6 with z6 = (e^{2 pi i/3} I_3, -I_2, e^{i pi/3}) (z6_entries gives the displayed entries), orderOf z6 = 6 (K = Z_6). faithful_quotient: the joint packet representation has kernel K = <z6> = ker(G~ -> S(U(3)xU(2))), and the descended representation of G~/K (QuotientGroup.kerLift of the units-valued hom) is injective, i.e. the packet is faithful precisely for G~/K, the group of thm:gauge-group (smGaugeQuotientEquiv). Proof follows the paper: e^c gives z^6 = 1, L gives g_2 = z^3 I = z^-3 I, d^c gives g_3 = z^2 I; then all seven act trivially on the central Z_6.

prop:finite-dirac.title: Canonical finite Dirac operator
prop:finite-dirac.note: Proved in the finite matrix rendering the paper's proof uses (disclosed): carrier C^n, grading Gamma (Gamma^H = Gamma, Gamma^2 = 1, P_pm = (1 pm Gamma)/2), self-adjoint full-cell generator A, D_F := P_- A P_+ + P_+ A P_- (finiteDirac). canonical_finite_dirac: (i) D_F is self-adjoint, grading-odd and equals the odd component (A - Gamma A Gamma)/2; (ii) uniqueness of the grading decomposition: any A = E + O with E even, O odd has O = D_F ('the odd component is fixed by the represented generator'); (iii) source minimality: with Pi the orthogonal projector onto the saturated represented range, odd-provenance completeness rendered as Pi D_F = D_F (supplied from zero odd-provenance defect by zeroOddProvenance_fixesFiniteDiracProjection), every self-adjoint generator B with the same represented action B Pi = D_F Pi and vanishing orthogonal innovation (1-Pi) B (1-Pi) = 0 equals D_F ('vanishing of the orthogonal odd innovation removes any additional grading-odd source'); (iv) typed contractions: for any typed resolution of the identity sum_t P_t = 1 by self-adjoint projectors (the eq:SM-types modules in one generation frame), the blocks Y_{tt'} = P_t D_F P_t' (Yukawa for t != t', Majorana for t = t') recover D_F = sum Y_{tt'}, pair as Y_{tt'}^H = Y_{t't}, and are grading-odd when the type projectors commute with Gamma. The 'reducing carrier' input of source saturation is the existing stabilizedIsometricCarrier_reduces. Not formalized: the specific SMST4 module list itself (the typed projectors are a parameter).

thm:structural-SM.title: Structural Standard-Model classification from a landed multiplicity packet
thm:structural-SM.note: Partial: an explicit-carrier assembly proves all six conclusions in one packet — (i) generated ∗-algebra on C^3⊕C^2⊕C⊕C equals M3⊕M2⊕C⊕C when the colour corner weight is positive, (ii) S(U(3)×U(2)) (kernel of the product determinant) ≅ (SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1))/Z6, (iii) anomaly classification 3a+2b=0, (iv) three-dimensional generation carrier, (v) normalized self-adjoint grading-odd Dirac seed with tight odd orbit and nonzero determinant seed, (vi) two independent non-orthogonal weak lines generate M2. thm:commutant-audit.note: Proved on finite matrix carriers: the commutator energy Σ‖[c_j,X]‖² vanishes exactly on the commutant (Ker ℒ = C'), and for X−P orthogonal to the commutant (P a commuting element, i.e. P = P_{C'}X) one has λ‖X−P‖²_HS ≤ Σ‖[c_j,X]‖² with λ the attained least eigenvalue of the positive-definite restricted commutator Gram (least positive eigenvalue of ℒ), the zero-complement case recorded separately. thm:howe-certificate.title: Positive certificate for the exact multiplicity algebra
thm:howe-certificate.note: Proved for finite matrix tuples: with M ⊆ ker(joint commutator) (i.e. M ⊆ C*(c)'), positivity of the commutator Gram on M^⊥ is equivalent to ker = M, the kernel is identified with the tuple commutant, and the least eigenvalue of the restricted Gram is attained and coincides with the first positive eigenvalue of the commutant Laplacian (coercivity clause). thm:howe-discriminant.title: Howe enhancement discriminant and generic rigidity
thm:howe-discriminant.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: discriminant, Cauchy–Binet, minors, enhancement locus, polynomial family, open dense, measure zero, generic rigidity, real-analytic.

cor:howe-nullity.title: Determinantal nullity filtration

The identification C*(c(theta))' = M + ker D(theta) is the Howe setting of thm:howe-certificate (not re-derived here).

thm:finite-anchor.title: Finite-anchor stability
thm:finite-anchor.note: Proved on a common finite screened carrier C^n with the l2 operator norm (Matrix.Norms.L2Operator): C_X = sqrt(sum_j ||c_{j,X}||_op^2) (opNormBudget), eps_{X,X0} = sqrt(sum_j ||c_{j,X}-c_{j,X0}||_op^2) (opNormDisplacement). Hypotheses: M commutes with both tuples (M <= ker of the joint HS commutator), anchor floor gamma_0 ||x||^2 <= ||J_{c0} x||^2 on M^perp, and 4(C_X+C_X0) eps < gamma_0. Conclusion: ker J_c = M (C*(c_X)' = M, also in matrix-commutant form), floor gamma_0 - 4(C_X+C_X0) eps > 0 on M^perp (lambda^+_min bound), and the Howe spectral-margin record. The quadratic-form perturbation bound previously assumed is now derived: ||A X||_HS <= ||A||_op ||X||_HS, ||X A||_HS <= ||A||_op ||X||_HS, ||[A,X]||_HS <= 2||A||_op||X||_HS, ||d_c|| <= 2C, ||d_c - d_c0|| <= 2 eps, |a^2-b^2| = |a-b|(a+b).

def:transported-mosco.title: Transported Mosco convergence

thm:cofinal-duality.title: Compact-Mosco cofinal spacetime--gauge duality

Scoped hypotheses differ in form from (H1)–(H4): Mosco convergence is rendered as strong resolvent convergence on a dense source set toward a bounded limit operator A with Ker A = M_∞, asymptotic compactness as compact graph-screen tails, and H is assumed infinite-dimensional.

The 'consequently' clause (external isotypic multiplicities constant for s >= r) is flat_word_span_multiplicity_constant: any function of the subspace V_s is constant for s >= r (disclosed: multiplicities are taken as functions of the subspace, not tied to a specific representation datum). Scoped: finite-dimensional E, arbitrary letter index type.

cor:flat-multiplicity-obstruction.title: Terminating multiplicity obstruction
cor:flat-multiplicity-obstruction.note: Proved, generalizing Predictive/FlatDepthColourObstruction.lean (trivial type, n = 3) to an arbitrary external type lambda and factor size n. Rendering (disclosed): the lambda-multiplicity space of a carrier V is the intertwiner space M_lambda(V) = Hom_G(W, V) for the external type sigma on W (multSpace), m_{lambda,s} = dim Hom_G(W, V_s) (mult); by thm:active-isotypic the lambda-block of the relative commutant is End(M_lambda(V_s)) = M_{m}(C) and an internal M_n(C) factor carried by it is a unital algebra hom M_n(C) -> End(M_lambda(V_s)) (the obstruction is proved for any injective linear map, which covers unital homs when n >= 1 and the multiplicity space is nonzero). Statement: at a flat word depth r (dim V_{r+1} <= dim V_r, or literally rank K_r = rank K_{r+1} for Grams of labelled spanning families), m_{lambda,r} < n implies V_s = V_r for all s >= r, m_{lambda,s} < n at every depth s, and no depth carries an internal M_n(C) factor on the lambda-multiplicity space (n^2 <= m^2 forces n <= m). The external action need not be a group representation in Lean (any families rho, sigma of operators).

prop:router-failure-locus.title: Algebraic structure of the router failure set

prop:bridge-router-residuals.title: Minimal bridge and weak-router residuals
prop:bridge-router-residuals.note: Proved. thm:finite-internal-landing-alternative.title: Finite internal landing alternative
thm:finite-internal-landing-alternative.note: Proved as the conjunction of the four branch implications with their finite witnesses plus the dimension table (the paper's 'exactly one outcome applies' is the decision-tree reading of these implications, whose hypotheses are the successive branch tests). (A1) = cor:flat-multiplicity-obstruction with n = 3 (FlatMultiplicityObstruction.lean; stated for a general external type lambda, the paper's external-trivial type being the special case): at a flat depth with m_{lambda,r} < 3 no injective linear map / unital hom M_3(C) -> End(M_lambda(V_s)) exists at any depth s. (A2) on the displayed three-space T + H_priv: if every represented bridge u in a family U has delta_col(u) = 0, Algebra.adjoin of p_T, the private matrix units and all u, u* is exactly the reducible block algebra M_2 + C (InternalSeed.blockDiag), hence not M_3. (A3) if all pairs of represented rank-one carriers on the weak plane have delta_wk = 0, the generated algebra is commutative (Algebra.commute_of_mem_adjoin_of_forall_mem_commute). (A4) on the census (3,2,1,1) carrier C^3+C^2+C+C in the concrete model of InternalDeficitAlternativesExact.lean: a colour-supported bridge with omega7 > 0 and a unit weak router h with delta_wk(e_3, h) > 0 (router_iff_weakResidual_pos identifies this with that file's Router h) give Algebra.adjoin(baseGens, u, u*, |h><h|) = the full block algebra M_3+M_2+C+C of dimension 15; as in the ledger entry of thm:internal-deficit-alternatives, the identification of this block algebra with the external relative commutant A'_ext at the census (thm:active-isotypic) is not part of the statement. Dimension table 9/11/13/15 = InternalDeficit.internal_deficit_alternatives. Depends on the (untracked, concurrently maintained) InternalDeficitAlternativesExact.lean names adjoin_both_eq_blockAlgebra / finrank_both / internal_deficit_alternatives / Router / WeakSupported / baseGens / bridgeGens / routerGen.

prop:det-incidence.title: Determinant-incidence line
prop:det-incidence.note: Proved in explicit oriented orthonormal up-incidence coordinates (colour index, two weak indices, Λ²C* pair label): 𝔄_det(Θ_τ)=τ, ‖Θ_τ‖²_HS = 6‖τ‖², Θ∘𝔄_det is the identity on the fully alternating line, and the alternating shadow is nonzero (m_det>0) iff a nonzero determinant seed occurs. Scoped: the fully alternating line is defined as the image of Θ, so the inverse-isomorphism clause reduces to the retraction identity.

thm:finite-action-identities.title: Finite Ward, BRST, and stress identities
thm:finite-action-identities.note: Partial: the four-term face/edge/vertex action is defined with definitional one-cell locality, its exact gauge invariance is derived from covariance of the cell densities (taken as hypotheses), the Ward identity D_U^*J + R^*E = 0 and the stress transfer L_q^*T = 2L_Φ^*E are derived by the chain rule from invariance of a generic finite action along gauge/relabeling flows, and a finite (group-cochain) BRST differential is proved nilpotent through ghost degree two. Missing: gauge covariance of the concrete Yang–Mills–Higgs–Dirac–Yukawa densities is assumed, the ghost-field BRST operator s (sc=−c², sU=c_tU−Uc_s, ...) with s²=0 in all degrees and sS=0 is not the formalized object, and the cutoff-independence of the support radius is only the definitional locality.
thm:finite-action-identities.plan: Ward and stress identities are derived abstractly (Gravity/FiniteActionWardBRSTStressEinsteinExact.lean:gauge_ward_divergence, relabeling_stress_transfer) and gauge invariance of the four-term action follows from covariance hypotheses (StandardModel/ExplicitRegulatedStandardModelActionExact.lean:explicitRegulatedStandardModelAction_gaugeInvariant). Missing: (1) proving covariance of the concrete Yang–Mills/Higgs/Dirac/Yukawa cell densities under U_e ↦ g_t U_e g_s⁻¹ etc. (finite, medium: trace cyclicity and unitary invariance on lattice cells); (2) the ghost BRST operator s with sc=−c², sU=c_tU−Uc_s, s²=0 in all ghost degrees and sS=0 — the library only has the group-cochain differential (finiteBRST2_nilpotent), and a faithful encoding needs a Grassmann-graded field algebra (ExteriorAlgebra-valued ghosts and a graded derivation), a new structure whose statement must be reformulated before it can be proved. Rated hard for the BRST clause; the covariance clause alone is medium.

cor:internal-vacuum.title: Stationary internal vacuum
cor:internal-vacuum.note: Proved: for the concrete regulated Standard-Model action (nonnegative couplings, unit reference doublet h₀) every directional derivative along every affine field line vanishes at the invariant vacuum U=I, H=v_H h₀, Ψ=Ψ̄=0, and the stabilizer of the nonzero reference weak doublet inside S(U(3)×U(2)) (kernel of the product determinant) is canonically isomorphic to U(3). Scoped: the stabilizer is computed for the reference doublet (0,1) (any v_H>0 h₀ is gauge equivalent); the cosmetic identification U(3) ≅ (SU(3)×U(1)_em)/Z3 is not separately formalized.

lem:mosco-strong-resolvent.title: Mosco convergence gives strong transported resolvents
lem:mosco-strong-resolvent.note: Proved on varying Hilbert systems: cofinal Mosco convergence of the closed forms (operator-graph energies q_X(A)=‖A_X A‖² on their domains) together with the weak resolvent equations for R_X, R_∞ gives strong operator convergence J_X R_X J_X^* f → J_∞ R_∞ J_∞^* f at every positive shift λ (the paper's λ=1). Scoped: Mosco convergence is required after every cofinal reindexing (CofinalMoscoConverges) and the forms are graph energies of closed operators.

lem:collective-compactness.title: Asymptotic compactness gives collective compactness
lem:collective-compactness.note: Proved in the form the paper's proof establishes, on the varying-Hilbert System carrier with def:asymptotic-compactness = System.AsymptoticallyCompact / LimitFormCompact (TransportedMoscoAsymptoticCompactness.lean). Resolvent vectors R_n f = (L_n+I)^{-1} J_n^* f are encoded as minimizers of the paper's objective F_{n,f}(u) = q_n(u) + ||u||^2 - 2 Re<J_n u, f> (only the comparison with u = 0 is used, plus q_n(0) = 0 and R_n f in the form domain); this yields eq:resolvent-energy-bound as ||R_n f||^2 + q_n(R_n f) <= 8||f||^2. Then (i) for bounded sources f_n the outputs J_n R_n f_n have a strongly convergent subsequence; (ii) the transported resolvents are sequentially collectively compact (one output per stage: SeqCollectivelyCompact, which is what the paper's proofs of this lemma and of lem:collective-norm use, and which is implied by the compact-container CollectivelyCompact of VaryingHilbertCollectiveCompactness.lean); (iii) the limiting resolvent J_inf R_inf is a compact operator (from LimitFormCompact). Disclosed gap: the compact-container form of collective compactness does not follow from the paper's one-member-per-stage definition alone (counterexample q_X = X||.||^2 on a fixed infinite-dimensional H: asymptotically compact, but no stage resolvent (X+1)^{-1} I is compact); collectivelyCompact_of_seq_of_stage_compact derives it under the extra hypotheses that the sequential property holds along every strictly monotone reindexing and every stage operator is compact.

lem:collective-norm.title: Collectively compact self-adjoint convergence is norm convergence
lem:collective-norm.note: Proved on a fixed Hilbert space: a collectively compact sequence of bounded symmetric operators converging strongly to T has compact limit T and ‖T_X − T‖_op → 0. Scoped: symmetry of the limit is listed as a hypothesis in the primed version (it follows trivially from strong convergence) and the unprimed version takes compactness of T as input.

prop:app-compact-mosco.title: Proof of compact Mosco resolvent convergence
prop:app-compact-mosco.note: Proved: cofinal Mosco convergence of operator-graph energies with weak resolvent equations (strong transported resolvents) plus a compact graph-screen tail (collective compactness) gives ‖R_X − R_∞‖_op → 0 with R_∞ compact, assembled through the strong-to-norm upgrade of lem:collective-norm. Scoped: asymptotic form compactness is rendered as the compact-screen tail condition on the embedded unit-ball outputs of the graph resolvents.

lem:low-spectrum-convergence.title: Low-spectrum convergence
lem:low-spectrum-convergence.note: Partial: the circle-contour Riesz projections Π_X(Γ) = (2πi)^{-1}∮_Γ (z−R_X)^{-1}dz converge in operator norm under norm convergence R_X → R_∞ with uniform resolvent bounds on Γ, and norm-convergent finite-rank idempotents have eventually equal range dimension. Missing: the ordered eigenvalue convergence μ_{k,X} → μ_{k,∞}, λ_{k,X} → λ_{k,∞} for every fixed index is not formalized.
lem:low-spectrum-convergence.plan: The Riesz-projection and rank clauses are proved (OperatorLimits/RieszProjectionStability.lean:circleRieszProjection_tendsto, NearbyProjectionRankStability.lean:eventually_finrank_range_eq_of_tendsto). Missing: ordered eigenvalue convergence μ_{k,X} → μ_{k,∞} for compact self-adjoint operators under norm convergence, which requires an ordered enumeration of eigenvalues with multiplicity and a min–max/Weyl perturbation inequality in infinite dimension — not in Mathlib (only finite-dimensional eigenvalues_antitone and Analysis/ApproximationSingularValues.lean:approximationNumber_weyl for approximation numbers). One route: prove μ_k equals the k-th approximation number for compact positive self-adjoint operators (needs the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators, absent), then use approximationNumber_weyl. Infrastructure-level.

prop:protected-kernel-locking.title: Protected-kernel locking
prop:protected-kernel-locking.note: Proved: with compact symmetric cutoff resolvents whose kernel-circle Riesz projections converge in norm (supplied by compact Mosco convergence) and protected subspaces M_X ⊆ Ker ℒ_X of the fixed rank m = dim Ker ℒ_∞, eventually M_X = Ker ℒ_X and the protected orthogonal projections converge in operator norm; the convergence of the attained first positive eigenvalue λ_{m+1}(ℒ_X) → λ_{m+1}(ℒ_∞) > 0 is proved for the commutant-Laplacian (joint-commutator) families the proposition is applied to. Scoped: the gap-convergence clause is formalized for joint-commutator families only, not for an arbitrary closed form.

prop:one-gen-incidence.title: Incidence reduces the one-generation commutant
prop:one-gen-incidence.note: Proved on the explicit carrier Fin 15 = Q(6)+u(3)+d(3)+L(2)+e(1) (sector15): with the gauge algebra encoded by all matrix units inside each sector (the paper's A_gauge = M6+M3+M3+M2+C from irreducible pairwise inequivalent modules) and three incidence matrices Y_e supported on the sector blocks Q x u, Q x d, L x e and nonzero, Algebra.adjoin C (gauge units, Y_e, Y_e*) equals the block algebra of the quark/lepton labelling (fibres of 12 and 3 vertices, i.e. M_12 + M_3), every element of its centralizer is diag(a.1_12, b.1_3) and the centralizer has finrank 2 (= C^2). The neutral-singlet variant on Fin 16 with a fourth nonzero L x nu incidence gives M_12 + M_4 with the same C^2 commutant. The engine is general: for any sectors beta : n -> B, incidence family Y and labelling kappa constant on sectors and incidence supports, adjoin = block algebra of kappa iff-style (adjoin_eq_labelAlgebra, via matrix units along walks of the vertex support graph), the commutant of a block algebra is the block-scalar diagonals with dimension = number of blocks, and reachability is transferred from the finite sector pattern graph (decided by `decide`).

thm:incidence-determinant.title: Positive incidence determinant and sufficient supports
thm:incidence-determinant.note: Proved. incidence_determinant (abstract setting of IncidencePolymatroidExact: constraint maps D_e : V -> W_e on finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces, G_e = D_e^* D_e, P_E = det(sum_e X_e [G_e]) in C[X_e]): (1) P_E homogeneous of degree n = dim V (IncidenceDeterminantExact); (2) every coefficient of P_E is a nonnegative real (incidencePoly_coeff_nonneg, 0 <= coeff in the complex order) via a symmetrised Cauchy-Binet identity proved from scratch (factorial_mul_det_eq_sum: n! det(sum_r t_r conj(A_ri) A_rj) = sum over ALL row choices p : Fin n -> R of (prod_i t_{p i}) |det A_p|^2, non-injective p contributing 0, so no grouping by image is needed), applied to the stacked matrix of the constraint vectors v_{(e,k)} = D_e^* b_{e,k}; (3) the face criterion P_E(w) > 0 <-> f(S) = n (<-> M(S) = M(E) in the commutant setting, incidenceDet_pos_iff_enlargedCommutant_eq); (4) under f(E) = n, the least power of X_e in P_E is exactly kappa_e = n - f(E minus e): kappa_e <= alpha(e) for every monomial with nonzero coefficient (a row basis uses at most f(E minus e) rows from the other blocks) and some monomial attains it (extend a row basis of R(E minus e) by rows of block e, via exists_linearIndepOn_extension); (5) e essential (f(E minus e) < n) iff every monomial of P_E contains X_e. Disclosures: the least-power clause carries the hypothesis f(E) = n (the paper's implicit G_E > 0; otherwise P_E = 0); 'w_e divides P_E' is rendered as 'every monomial with nonzero coefficient has X_e-exponent >= 1' rather than via MvPolynomial divisibility.

prop:deletion-margin.title: Exact simultaneous-deletion margin
prop:deletion-margin.note: Proved in the setting of IncidencePolymatroidExact (base commutant M₀, constraint maps D_e, residual space V, restricted maps D_e|_V) with G_e = (D_e|_V)*(D_e|_V) as operators V →L[ℂ] V (a C*-algebra), G^{1/2} = CFC.sqrt G, G^{-1/2} = Ring.inverse, B_e = G^{-1/2}G_eG^{-1/2}. G = G_E is automatically positive definite on V (gram_residualGram_univ_injective, from M(E)∩V = 0). deletion_margin: ∑B_e = I; G_{E∖R} = G^{1/2}(I−B_R)G^{1/2} (eq:deletion-factor); 0 ⪯ B_R ⪯ I; the boxed eq:deletion-margin `enlargedCommutant M₀ D (univ \ R) = fullCommutant M₀ D ↔ ‖B_R‖ < 1` with ‖·‖ the operator (C*) norm of V →L[ℂ] V (proof as in the paper: I−B_R invertible iff 1 ∉ spectrum of the positive contraction B_R iff ‖B_R‖<1, via CStarAlgebra.norm_mem_spectrum_of_nonneg, plus congruence by the bijective G^{1/2}); and for β_R = ‖B_R‖ < 1 the margins in quadratic-form terms: (1−β_R)Re⟨Gx,x⟩ ≤ Re⟨G_{E∖R}x,x⟩ for all x (this is G_{E∖R} ⪰ (1−β_R)G in the Loewner order) and every spectral lower bound λ‖x‖² ≤ Re⟨Gx,x⟩ yields (1−β_R)λ‖x‖² ≤ Re⟨G_{E∖R}x,x⟩ (i.e. λ_min(G_{E∖R}) ≥ (1−β_R)λ_min(G)). Scoped: V finite-dimensional (completeness supplied by a local instance); the generic section (gram, sqrtGram, bmat, …) works for any positive family with injective sum.

prop:word-space-inflation.title: Invariant word-space inflation without an internal $M_3$
prop:word-space-inflation.note: Proved. word_space_inflation, on the benchmark E = ordered unequal pairs of Fin 4 with the relabeling matrices Pm sigma: (1) the algebra generated by the point projections and the fibre averages T, H (Tm, Hm, entries 1/3 on same tail / same head) is M_12(C) (adjoin_gens_eq_top, via thm:connected-router: the support graph of the router T+H is connected, router_preconnected, explicit walks of length <= 3); (2) A^{S_4} = the commutant of the Pm sigma in A = M_12 (invariant_algebra_eq), which is isomorphic to C x M_2(C) x C x C (DegreeOneWedderburn.degreeOneCommutantEquiv); (3) the permutation character chi(sigma) = Tr Pm sigma (trace_Pm_eq_permChar; class values (12,2,0,0,0), permChar_classes) has character inner products (1/24) sum chi_lambda chi = (1,0,2,1,1) in the order (1, sgn, W, W x sgn, V_2) (physical_multiplicities); (4) the conjugation representation X -> P X P^{-1} on L^2(M_12) = M_E(C) has LinearMap.trace equal to chi(sigma)^2 (trace_conjRep, via Tr(X -> AXB) = Tr A Tr B, trace_mulLeft_comp_mulRight) with inner products (7,5,19,17,12) (conjugation_multiplicities); (5) its commutant contains an injective multiplicative M_7(C) block (WordSpaceFirewall.m7Block); (6) A^{S_4} admits no injective linear image of M_3(C). Disclosure: the five irreducible characters of S_4 are taken as the standard explicit class functions of ActiveResidualCensus (chi_W = fix - 1, chi_{V_2} = fixMatch - 1, chi_{W x sgn} = sgn (fix - 1), sgn, 1); multiplicities are rendered as the character inner products (kernel-checked over Z by decide), not through Mathlib's FDRep isotypic decomposition.

thm:subdirect-classification.title: Finite subdirect matrix-algebra classification
thm:subdirect-classification.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: subdirect, surjective coordinate projection, diagonal embedding up to inner automorphism, equal matrix size classes (GrandWedderburn.lean covers block commutants on a fixed decomposed carrier, not the subdirect-product classification).

prop:all-excursion-return.title: All-excursion return alternative
prop:all-excursion-return.note: Proved. all_excursion_return_of_mass_eq_zero: in the setting of thm:reciprocal-return (carrier T + H_priv + (V x N), covariant entries (v_g x I)A, reverse exits B*(v_g* x I), mediator I x h with h Hermitian, internal operations on T and H_priv, plus adjoints; words = generated multiplicative monoid), if m_ret = 0 at the horizon n = dim N then (1) N_A = Span{h^k Ran rho_A : k < n} and N_B = Span{h^k Ran rho_B : k < n} (cyclicSpace, subspaces of EuclideanSpace C N) are orthogonal (Submodule.IsOrtho), (2) the stopping projection Q = I_T + 0 + (I_V x P_{N_A}) with P_{N_A} the orthogonal projection onto N_A as a matrix (cyclicProj := toEuclideanLin.symm of starProjection) commutes with every generator of the bank and its adjoint, and (3) every word w has p_H w p_T = 0. Ingredients: Cayley-Hamilton gives h^k Ran rho in N_rho for every k (pow_mul_apply_mem), hence h-invariance; h self-adjoint makes the projection commute with h (starProjection_comm_of_invariant); P rho_A = rho_A; m_ret = 0 <-> rho_B h^k rho_A = 0 (mass_eq_zero_iff) gives P rho_B = 0 and N_A perp N_B. Scoped hypotheses as in ReciprocalReturnMassExact: finite index types, V nonempty, v a unitary representation of the finite group G irreducible in the Schur (scalar-commutant) form, h Hermitian.

thm:determinant-arity-floor.title: Sharp five-slot determinant-mode floor
thm:determinant-arity-floor.note: Formalised as weight bookkeeping on the graded basis: single-system carrier C⊕W₂⊕N (Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 2 ⊕ N, weights (1,0),(0,1),(0,0)), endWeightSupport w = {w i − w j} (the central-weight support of End), tensorWeight = slot sums on the diagonal k-fold carrier. determinant_arity_floor: support ⊆ {(0,0),±(1,0),±(0,1),±(1,−1)} (equality when N nonempty), (−3,−2) absent from the single-system support, absent on k-fold carriers for k<5 (total charge bound a,b≥0, a+b≤k), present at k=5 (line C⊗C⊗C⊗W₂⊗W₂ of weight (3,2) → neutral line). torusAction_conj_single proves that conjugating the matrix unit E_ij by the diagonal torus action diag(e^{i(aα+bβ)}) multiplies it by the character of w i − w j, so endWeightSupport is the actual central character support of the matrix units; det_weight_matrix_unit exhibits the k=5 rank-one map with character (−3,−2). Scoped: the k=5 presence needs a neutral line ([Nonempty N]), as in the paper's proof; the alternating line is represented by its weight (3,2) (any vector of the weight-(3,2) subspace, in particular det C·det W₂, has that weight) rather than constructed as an exterior power.

prop:five-kraus-freedom.note: Full statement on Matrix m m ℂ (finite-dimensional edge-system space) for a Helmert frame O given as a parameter with the three identities of eq:helmert-frame (structure HelmertFrame; the paper says 'choose O with ...', so the frame is a parameter, not constructed). six_edge_iff_five_kraus: eq:six-edge-normalization (∑K*K=I, ∑K=√2 I, K linearly independent) ⟺ ∃ B_1..B_5 with ∑B*B=I, I,B_1..B_5 linearly independent (Fin.cons 1 B) and K_e = I/√18 + √(2/3)∑O_{eμ}B_μ (normalForm). coarse_channel_normalForm: ∑K_e ρ K_e* = (1/3)ρ + (2/3)∑B_μ ρ B_μ*. starAdjoin_normalForm_eq: StarAlgebra.adjoin ℂ (range K) = StarAlgebra.adjoin ℂ (range B) (unital *-algebra generated = C*-algebra generated in finite dimension). five_kraus_freedom assembles all clauses with the explicit extraction B_μ = √(3/2)∑_e O_{eμ}K_e as in the paper's proof.

prop:record-witness.title: Record-complete nonidentifiability witness
prop:record-witness.note: Partial (first two claims of the proposition now proved for BOTH families; the rest open). Commuting family (RecordWitnessCommutingFamily, previous batch): H^c_e = diagonal sign involutions on the 20 three-subsets; K^c_e = I/sqrt18 + (i/3)H^c_e satisfy eq:six-edge-normalization and eq:matching-record-data (commuting_record_data), and the unital algebra generated by the H^c_e is the diagonal algebra C^20 (adjoin_Hc_eq_diagonal), i.e. C*(K^c) = C^20 (the K's and the H's generate the same unital algebra; this last trivial step is not written out). Each of (b)-(d) is a separate afternoon; (d) needs a Choi-matrix formalisation not yet in the library.

prop:ten-panel-reconstruction.title: Explicit ten-panel reconstruction
prop:ten-panel-reconstruction.note: Proved in the paper's concrete frame: accepted operators A_{e,a} = K_e ⊗ Q_a (TenPanel.acceptedOp), Gram M_ϑ = ϑI + (1−ϑ)cc* (coefficientGram) with the explicit positive square root √ϑ(I−P) + √h P identified with Mathlib's CFC.sqrt (cfc_sqrt_coefficientGram), frame coefficients C_ν = Σ_j (M_ϑ^{1/2})_{jν} A_j, Stinespring map V = Σ C_ν ⊗ |ν⟩, Heisenberg pullback 𝒫*(F) = V*(I⊗F)V, and eq:complementary-pullback 𝒫*(|z⟩⟨w|) = C(z)*C(w) proved for any finite coefficient family (complementaryPullback_vecMulVec). ten_panel_reconstruction gives both boxed formulas D_μ ⊗ I = (2√3/√(ϑh))(𝖷_μ + i𝖸_μ) and K_e = I/√18 + Σ_μ O_{eμ} D_μ; the manuscript's intermediate claims C(u) = √(h/12) I and C(r_μ) = (√ϑ/2) D_μ ⊗ I are the lemmas pulledCoefficient_uniformEnv / pulledCoefficient_contrastEnv; the 'determines the represented system algebra and commutant' clause is encoded as ten_panel_determines_coefficients (equal ten pullbacks ⇒ equal coefficient families, hence equal algebra and commutant). Scoped hypotheses (disclosed): H_E and H_R are finite-dimensional matrix spaces; 0 < ϑ < 1; only the parts of eq:six-edge-normalization / eq:helmert-frame that the proof uses are assumed (Σ_e K_e = √2 I, Σ_a Q_a = I, Oᵀ𝟏 = 0, OOᵀ = I − 𝟏𝟏ᵀ/6), so the theorem is slightly more general than stated; the Helmert frame O is a parameter.

prop:reconstruction-error.title: Robust commutant stopping test
prop:reconstruction-error.note: TenPanel.reconstruction_error proves all three clauses in the ten-panel frame: with measured panels X̂_μ, Ŷ_μ of Hilbert–Schmidt errors ε_{X,μ}, ε_{Y,μ} and the linear reconstruction D̂_μ = (2√3/√(ϑh))(X̂_μ + iŶ_μ), K̂_e = I/√18 + Σ_μ O_{eμ} D̂_μ (reconstructedCoefficient), (i) (Σ_e ‖K̂_e − K_e ⊗ I_R‖²_HS)^{1/2} ≤ e_K := (2√3/√(ϑh))(Σ_μ (ε_{X,μ}+ε_{Y,μ})²)^{1/2} (eq:appendix-reconstruction-error, via helmert_sum_norm_sq: OᵀO = I preserves the sum of squared errors); (ii) ‖(𝒟̂ − 𝒟)x‖ ≤ 2√2 e_K ‖x‖ for the star-closed stacked commutator maps jointCommutatorL2 (starClosedStack ·) (eq:appendix-commutator-error, via ‖A‖_op ≤ ‖A‖_HS and the existing jointCommutatorL2_sub_norm_le); (iii) if 𝒟̂ has least singular value ≥ ŝ on a protected complement W (ŝ‖x‖ ≤ ‖𝒟̂x‖ for x ∈ W) and ŝ > 2√2 e_K, then no nonzero x ∈ W lies in ker 𝒟 (generic versions: robust_commutant_stopping_test also gives the lower bound (ŝ − 2√2 e_K)‖x‖ ≤ ‖𝒟x‖ and the matrix form; robust_commutant_stopping_test_ker gives ker 𝒟 = M when W = Mᗮ for a verified protected M ⊆ ker 𝒟). Disclosed conventions: the reconstruction lives on the common carrier E × R, so the true coefficient compared against K̂_e is K_e ⊗ I_R (the paper writes K_e); the 'measured least singular value ŝ on the protected complement' is formalised as the bound ŝ‖x‖ ≤ ‖𝒟̂x‖ on W (equivalently ŝ ≤ σ_min(𝒟̂|_W)); hypotheses as in prop:ten-panel-reconstruction plus OᵀO = I.
